chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Muskān, from Zurārah and Abū Basīr, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who had a slave, and a goldsmith or someone else hired him from him: 'If he lost something or escaped from him, then his guardians are liable (for compensation).'
ai.seo_question: Who is liable if a hired slave loses an item or escapes?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on rentals, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a ruling originally attributed to Imam Ali (AS) regarding the liability of a slave's masters when the slave is hired out. It establishes that the guardians (mawālī) remain financially responsible for loss or escape, reflecting the classical Shia juristic view that the hirer bears the risk of use while the masters retain the risk of the asset's value and custody.
